identity.name: assert_coa_freshness
identity.description: CoA source freshness (portal-rot) ASSERT: one aggregate SELECT over coa_applications measures the days since the coa root last touched any row (MAX(last_seen_at), touched for every fed key) and grades it PASS / WARN / FAIL on two step-owned logic variables; an empty table WARNs (fresh staging, not portal rot). Read-only: no write, no recovery, no counters (the ASSERT profile).

why_lock.text: Ported verbatim from the pre-conversion `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 108` (scripts/quality/assert-coa-freshness.js:38, Bundle G Wave 6 retrofit cc2f5d5d), agreeing with src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts. Kept via identity.lock + the §5.4 source-text convention (declared, never read, in the frozen shell).

on_check_error_why.text: One aggregate SELECT feeds both checks; a query that throws means the step could not measure freshness at all, which must redden the run rather than read as a healthy or empty table (Spec 30 §5.4.1: an exception-derived failure halts). The pre-conversion step let the same error escape pipeline.run().

expect.reports: 1 when coa_applications has no rows, else 0

why.text: Ported from the empty-table lane (scripts/quality/assert-coa-freshness.js:68-81, b25945bb; kept WARN by WF2 P6.5 fb593a9e): an empty table is fresh staging, not portal rot, so it WARNs and never FAILs. The exact zero-tolerance answer (R-DF EXTERNALIZED: a count bound with no tunable). On an empty table ingestion_days_ago reports inert (INFO), so the verdict stays one WARN.

expect.reports: round((run clock - MAX(coa_applications.last_seen_at)) / 1 day), floored at 0; inert on an empty table

why.text: Ported from :85-94 (fcd6c300 measure ingestion not hearing_date; f1dca94f WF3-E5 externalized WARN; fb593a9e WF2 P6.5 FAIL tier). PASS <= assert_coa_freshness_warn_max_days, WARN <= assert_coa_freshness_fail_max_days, else FAIL (RE-FREEZE #7 warn_limit). ACF-D7 declared deviation: legacy compared >= (exclusive ceilings); value_max is inclusive, so exactly 45 (135) rounded days now reads PASS (WARN), one day later — the R-DC precedent (assert_data_bounds' boolcfg checks, operator y 2026-10-17). Values unchanged. Never blocking: legacy never halted the chain on portal rot.

deviations.from: Pre-conversion config refusal: the Zod refine `coa_freshness_fail_days > coa_freshness_warn_days` threw before the read (scripts/quality/assert-coa-freshness.js:34-36)

why.text: config.logic_variables[] carries independent per-variable bounds and no cross-variable relation, and a check that compares two ctx.config values inside its body is a compute-decides finding (R-BZ G7, R-DC). A misordered pair degrades safely in the two-tier check: when fail_max < warn_max, any value above warn_max is above fail_max too, so it reads FAIL (the stricter tier wins); nothing reads PASS that legacy would not. Recorded as ACF-D8.

limitations.what: The metric is the coa root's ingestion touch, so it measures whether the LOADER ran, not whether the city published anything new: the coa root touches last_seen_at for every fed key (R-DW keeps it), so a frozen CKAN feed that is still served reads fresh. Portal content staleness is the coa root's own max_days_stale row.
limitations.measured: scripts/load-coa.js:565-582 (the every-fed-key touch); DB 2026-10-18 MAX(last_seen_at) 2026-10-16 13:57 UTC after the H6 --full runs.

why.text: The generic runner (scripts/lib/step/index.js) emits the declared lock_held_elsewhere terminal on advisory-lock contention; the pre-conversion step returned bare with no step-level emit (:139).

A WARN row stands (portal slow, or an empty table) and nothing FAILED, so selectTerminal picks this success terminal by the real status (COMPLETED_WITH_WARNINGS); checks_passed is 'all' only when errors and warnings are both empty, so a WARN run never carries it (the assert_data_bounds form, MQ-A4 (a)).

Non-halting by design: an ingestion_days_ago FAIL (portal likely dead) reddens the row-derived verdict but the run completes, as the pre-conversion step did (:106-107 logged, never threw). Distinguishes from failed_check_error below.
execution.on_check_error fail_step: the aggregate SELECT threw, so freshness could not be measured ("I could not check" never reads as healthy, Spec 30 §5.4.1).
